Chapter 18PROCESSING

Far Shore

Some things only make sense from across the water.

Across Burrard Inlet, the lights of North Vancouver climb the lower slopes of the mountains. On the right night, seen from this side of the water, they arrange themselves into long flowing shapes, like a script in a language nobody here speaks.

Cross the bridge and they are apartments again. That is not a trick. Some things cannot be understood up close. They only resolve after a distance has been crossed: water, language, a different way of living, a few kilometres of dark. The Far Shore is where the things the city cannot understand are turned into things it can use, and the water in between is what does the work.

The Probes send their unknowns across to it. What comes back sounds different on the wires for weeks. Nobody on either side has ever read the lights aloud, and they never spell anything. They only resolve, and only from the other side.

The ruleThe message only resolves from the other side of the water.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
